background.text: What D2 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When the Property Owner confirms the deletion, the Property record must be removed from the Platform (represented by the record not being retained in the database).

rules.text: WHEN a Property Owner initiates property deletion, THE Platform SHALL prompt for confirmation before proceeding
rules.reading: Whenever a Property Owner initiates the deletion of a property, the Platform must display a confirmation prompt before proceeding with the deletion.

rules.text: WHEN a Property Owner confirms deletion, THE Platform SHALL remove the Property record from the Platform
rules.reading: Whenever a property owner confirms the deletion of a property, the platform must remove the property record from the platform.

rules.text: WHEN a Property is deleted, THE Platform SHALL display a confirmation message and redirect to the properties list
rules.reading: When a property has been successfully deleted, the platform must display a confirmation message and redirect the user to the properties list page.

rules.text: THE Platform SHALL implement soft deletion to retain Property records in the database for audit purposes while hiding them from the user interface
rules.reading: Whenever a Property is successfully deleted, the Platform must retain its record in the database for audit purposes and hide it from the user interface.

alternative.reading: The requirement mandates that the platform uses soft deletion, meaning property records must be retained in the database for audit purposes while being hidden from the user interface.

rules.text: WHEN a Property Owner attempts to delete a Property that does not belong to their User Account, THE Platform SHALL deny the deletion and display an authorization error message
rules.reading: If a property owner attempts to delete a property that is not associated with their user account, the platform must deny the deletion request and display an authorization error message.
